newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli president to visit Jordan soon.
newsitem.headline: Israeli president to visit Jordan soon.

text.p: Israeli President Ezer Weizman will visit Jordan in the coming weeks, an official said, to try to defuse mounting tension over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's handling of Middle East peace talks.

Weizman, whose presidential role is largely ceremonial, has placed himself at the centre of Israel's diplomatic activity, this week meeting Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and planning talks with President Hosni Mubarak in Cairo on Monday.
"He was invited (to Jordan) long ago. The visit will probably come about in the next week or two," a presidential spokeswoman told Reuters.

Netanyahu's hardline positions have strained relations with much of the Arab world including Jordan, the only Arab neighbour that did not express alarm at the election of the new Israeli leader last May.
Jordan's King Hussein, who signed a peace agreement with Israel in 1994 and is seen as the Jewish state's closest Arab ally, warned Netanyahu this week that his policies could lead to war.

The Israeli Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper said Weizman, a former defence minister and one of the architects of Israel's 1979 peace accord with Egypt, was coordinating his diplomatic efforts with the prime minister's office but some officials were uneasy about his activity.
